steps.label: Nodal map
steps.detail: Assign every source node/group actual side and descriptive location using the explicitly named map/version, acquired boundaries and coverage limits.
steps.look: Use actual acquired skull-base/lower-neck extent, planes and map-specific boundaries such as glands, muscles, hyoid, cricoid and vessels. Extended radiotherapy and surgical labels are not interchangeable; record descriptive location for every unassigned or differently defined region.
findings: Every actual source side/descriptive group/node [ ]; map/version/level or unresolved assignment [ ].
Retropharyngeal/parotid/other source region [ ]; named convention and actual boundaries [ ].
steps.tip: Name the map and version. A level number in one surgical/extended radiotherapy convention cannot silently become the same compartment in another; unknown boundaries remain unassigned.

steps.label: Index nodes
steps.detail: Inventory actual covered nodes/components and distribution; index-node measurements do not replace all obtained nodal or non-nodal extent.
steps.look: Trace every actual covered node/group and conglomerate component, including tiny or normal-sized but morphologically concerning nodes. Measure source-resolved local short/long axes with node identity, site, sequence/phase, calibration and comparison; selected index nodes do not quantify all burden.
findings: Each index node/component with actual identity/local axes/source measurement [ ].
Actual obtained distribution/coalescence and unresolved burden [ ].
steps.tip: Small size or a preserved visible feature does not prove benignity or exclude microscopic metastasis. Size thresholds and index-node choices depend on the actual disease/level and source context.

steps.label: Nodal morphology
steps.detail: Describe each source-resolved nodal margin/cortex/hilum/content and actual signal/contrast/diffusion or ultrasound findings with uncertainty and differential.
steps.look: Inspect each actual source margin, cortical/hilar/content component, necrotic-appearing/cystic/calcific area and adjacent node. CT/MRI contrast/DWI/ADC, ultrasound cortex/hilum and Doppler are separate acquired sources; a permitted modality does not supply unperformed measurements or tissue identity.
findings: Source cystic/necrotic-appearing/hilar/cortical/calcium or other component [ ]; differential and supplied tissue/assay information [ ].
Actual acquired contrast/DWI/ADC/US/Doppler details and unavailable source information [ ].
steps.tip: Cystic adult lateral-neck nodes/masses require an appropriate differential and clinical/tissue evaluation; neither benign congenital cyst nor unique metastatic/HPV/thyroid identity is established from morphology alone.

steps.label: Extranodal extension and vessels
steps.detail: Trace source nodal-to-fat/adjacent-node/muscle/skin/gland/vascular interfaces; separate imaging suspicion from supplied pathological ENE and vascular function.
steps.look: Assess all source-supported adjacent tissue and vascular contacts, fat-plane/capsular appearances, coalescent components and obtained extent. Record actual source technique, uncertainty and comparison. Contact/stranding or matting alone is not pathological ENE, vessel invasion, thrombosis, flow loss or surgical resectability.
findings: Source margin/adjacent tissue/vascular relation [ ]; imaging ENE suspicion and confidence [ ].
Actual carotid/venous contact/phase/source measurement and unassessed wall/patency/function [ ].
Pathological ENE if supplied [ ]; not established solely by imaging [ ].
steps.tip: Imaging-detected ENE is distinct from pathological ENE. Use actual applicability and source criteria with confidence; post-treatment inflammation, unresolved borders and vessel contact require explicit limits.

steps.label: Primary site and staging pathway
steps.detail: Review actual covered primary-site/airway/other tissue and supplied clinical/tissue/assay/staging context; morphology alone does not identify a primary, organism or molecular category.
steps.look: Review only actually covered mucosal/tonsillar/tongue-base/laryngeal, thyroid/salivary and other source sites. Record supplied primary/treatment/surgery/biopsy/HPV or other assay dates separately. Any staging system/version/category needs the confirmed applicable clinical/tissue context and all required source findings.
findings: Every covered primary-site/airway/other tissue finding and unassessed extent [ ].
Supplied primary/assay/treatment evidence and applicable staging system/version [ ]; unresolved components [ ].
steps.tip: Absent visible primary in limited imaging is not exclusion of an occult primary. Assay/organism/histology and primary-specific stage are supplied evidence, not geometry or generic nodal patterns.

model.reporting_aim: Partial neck orientation only. This schematic does not supply every native patient node/level boundary, cortex/hilum/capsule or extranodal/vascular interface, microscopic metastasis, primary/assay identity, stage or flow. Actual acquired sources and unassessed anatomy remain explicit.

steps.label: Space of origin
steps.detail: Localise the epicentre to a named space above or below the hyoid.
steps.look: Axial T1 without fat suppression to see preserved fat planes; identify the parapharyngeal fat as the key landmark.
findings: Lesion centred in the [parapharyngeal / masticator / parotid / carotid / retropharyngeal / perivertebral / visceral] space.
Lesion extends from the suprahyoid to the infrahyoid neck.
steps.tip: The direction in which the parapharyngeal fat is displaced tells you the space of origin.

steps.label: Tissue characteristics
steps.detail: Describe composition, T1 and T2 signal, diffusion and enhancement.
steps.look: T1, T2, fat-suppressed post-contrast images and DWI.
findings: T2-bright, well-defined lesion with heterogeneous enhancement (pleomorphic adenoma pattern).
Flow voids with intense enhancement (paraganglioma: salt-and-pepper pattern).
Restricted diffusion with homogeneous enhancement (lymphoma pattern).
Non-enhancing fluid (cyst).

steps.label: Displacement pattern
steps.detail: Assess how fat planes and the carotid and jugular vessels are displaced.
steps.look: Axial images at the level of maximal lesion size.
findings: Parapharyngeal fat displaced [anteromedially / posterolaterally].
Carotid artery displaced anteriorly (post-styloid / carotid space lesion).
Internal and external carotid arteries splayed (carotid body paraganglioma).
steps.tip: Splaying of the internal and external carotid arteries at the bifurcation indicates a carotid body tumour.

steps.label: Spread and critical structures
steps.detail: Assess airway, skull base, perineural pathways and visceral extension.
steps.look: Coronal images to the skull base; foramina and nerves; airway calibre.
steps.normal: No airway compromise; skull base and neural pathways intact.
findings: Extension to the skull base through the [foramen ovale].
Airway narrowed to __ mm.
Invasion of the [larynx / thyroid].

steps.label: Nodes and complications
steps.detail: Review regional nodes, collections and venous thrombosis.
steps.look: Nodal levels; rim-enhancing collections; jugular veins.
steps.normal: No suspicious nodes, collection or thrombosis.
findings: Suspicious nodes at level [ ].
Retropharyngeal abscess __ mm with rim enhancement.
Internal jugular vein thrombosis.

model.reporting_aim: Relate the mass to the midline, hyoid, sternocleidomastoid and carotid space before describing its content.

steps.label: Location
steps.detail: Localise the mass relative to the midline, hyoid and neck spaces, with the child's age.
steps.look: Ultrasound first: midline versus lateral; relation to the hyoid, sternocleidomastoid and thyroid.
findings: Midline cystic mass at the level of the hyoid.
Lateral cystic mass anterior to the sternocleidomastoid at the angle of the mandible.
Posterior triangle multiloculated mass.
steps.tip: Location is the strongest clue: midline suggests thyroglossal duct or dermoid cyst; anterior to sternocleidomastoid suggests a second branchial cleft cyst.

steps.label: Composition
steps.detail: Describe cystic or solid components, septa, debris and calcification.
steps.look: Ultrasound with high-frequency probe; MRI for deep extension.
findings: Unilocular cyst with thin wall and internal debris.
Multiloculated cystic mass with fluid levels (lymphatic malformation).
Solid mass with calcification (pilomatrixoma / teratoma / neuroblastoma).

steps.label: Vascularity
steps.detail: Assess internal and peripheral flow or enhancement and vessel relationships.
steps.look: Colour Doppler; contrast MRI when performed.
findings: Avascular cyst.
Hypervascular solid mass (infantile haemangioma pattern).
Venous malformation with phleboliths and slow flow.

steps.label: Anatomic connections
steps.detail: Look for a tract, gland of origin or other structural connection, and airway effect.
steps.look: Relation to the hyoid, thyroid, salivary glands and sternocleidomastoid.
findings: Cyst embedded in the strap muscles with a tract to the hyoid (thyroglossal duct cyst).
Fusiform enlargement of the sternocleidomastoid in an infant (fibromatosis colli).
Ectopic thyroid tissue with an empty thyroid bed.
steps.tip: Confirm a normal thyroid in its bed before a midline mass is removed; it may be the only thyroid tissue.

steps.label: Nodes and infection
steps.detail: Assess nodal patterns and inflammatory complications such as abscess.
steps.look: Nodes: hilum, shape, necrosis; surrounding fat; collections.
findings: Suppurative lymphadenitis with abscess __ mm.
Necrotic nodes with minimal surrounding inflammation (atypical mycobacterial pattern).
Multiple enlarged nodes without hila (lymphoma to be considered).

steps.label: Primary site
steps.detail: Identify the lesion epicentre, subsite and dimensions.
steps.look: Contrast-enhanced MRI or CT; separate tumour from retained secretions on T2 and post-contrast images.
findings: Mass in the [ ] measuring __ × __ × __ mm.
Enhancing tumour separate from T2-bright retained secretions in the obstructed sinus.
steps.tip: On MRI, retained secretions are T2-bright and non-enhancing; tumour is intermediate and enhances.

steps.label: Growth pattern and local invasion
steps.detail: Inspect fat planes, muscle, bone and cartilage, and whether growth is expansile or destructive.
steps.look: Bone windows on CT; T1 marrow signal on MRI.
findings: Destructive bone erosion (aggressive growth pattern).
Smooth expansile remodelling (slow-growing lesion).
Invasion of the [pterygoid muscles / orbit / cartilage].
steps.tip: Bone destruction suggests malignancy; smooth remodelling suggests a slow benign process such as a mucocele.

steps.label: Perineural spread
steps.detail: Review neural pathways and skull-base foramina for spread.
steps.look: Pterygopalatine fossa, foramen rotundum and ovale, Meckel cave; fat-suppressed post-contrast MRI.
findings: Obliteration of fat in the pterygopalatine fossa with enhancement along V2.
Enlargement and enhancement of the [ ] nerve through the foramen [ ].
steps.tip: Loss of fat in the pterygopalatine fossa is an early sign of perineural spread.

steps.label: Vessels and airway
steps.detail: Assess vessel encasement and airway compromise.
steps.look: Carotid arteries and internal jugular veins; airway calibre.
steps.normal: No vascular encasement or airway compromise.
findings: Carotid encasement of more than 270°.
Airway narrowed to __ mm.

steps.label: Nodes and other sites
steps.detail: Map regional nodes by level and look for additional lesions.
steps.look: Nodal levels I–V and retropharyngeal nodes.
steps.normal: No suspicious nodes; no second lesion.
findings: Necrotic level [II] node __ mm.
Cystic node from HPV-associated oropharyngeal carcinoma.
Second primary in the [ ].

steps.label: Globes and preseptal tissues
steps.detail: Describe each actually covered globe, lens, intraocular and preseptal component with source side, extent, technique and uncertainty.
steps.look: Review original acquired planes/windows/sequences, coverage and artifact. Follow globe contour, lens position and source-resolved vitreous/retinal/choroidal or other intraocular components, foreign material and preseptal tissue. Unresolved thin layers and small injuries remain explicit.
findings: Source globe contour/volume or intraocular material change [ ]; injury differential and clinical assessment [ ].
Each source foreign material location/type uncertainty and actual MRI safety assessment [ ].
Source retinal/choroidal or other intraocular finding and unresolved layers [ ].
steps.tip: Record actual MRI safety assessment/clearance when metallic foreign material is a concern; no model or teaching image clears a patient for MRI. Source contour change or material appearance needs appropriate clinical/ophthalmic correlation.

steps.label: Orbital compartments
steps.detail: Localise every actual lesion/collection to its obtained preseptal, extraconal, conal, intraconal or other compartment and trace source boundaries/relationships.
steps.look: Trace every lesion component, capsule/margin or unresolved boundary against the globe, muscle cone, lacrimal region, nerve and wall. Record actual CT/MRI contrast phase, DWI/ADC and comparison if supplied; a selected static image does not establish enhancement kinetics, whole extent or unique histology.
findings: Each source collection/lesion compartment, component and obtained extent [ ]; differential [ ].
Actual acquired enhancement phases or DWI/ADC information [ ]; unresolved kinetics/calibration [ ].
Lacrimal/preseptal or other source tissue component [ ].
steps.tip: Static enhancement, DWI brightness and compartment location do not uniquely establish abscess, vascular lesion or tumour. Quantitative diffusion and time-dependent filling need their actual acquired ADC/phase sources.

steps.label: Muscles and optic nerves
steps.detail: Review each source-resolved extraocular muscle/tendon and optic nerve/sheath component; morphology does not alone establish endocrine/inflammatory/neoplastic identity or function.
steps.look: Assess every actual muscle belly/tendon/insertion, optic nerve/sheath and available surrounding fat on resolving acquired planes. Record signal/enhancement, compression or other morphology with uncertainty. Tendon sparing or tram-track appearance has overlap and cannot supply a unique diagnosis or measured visual function.
findings: Every actual muscle belly/tendon/insertion change [ ]; differential and acquired sources [ ].
Optic nerve/sheath signal/enhancement or compression morphology [ ]; clinical function kept separate [ ].
steps.tip: Muscle/tendon and optic nerve/sheath patterns overlap across conditions. Imaging displacement, thickening or enhancement does not by itself measure vision, motility, optic neuropathy or a unique tissue diagnosis.

steps.label: Orbital apex and intracranial extension
steps.detail: Trace actual acquired orbital-apical, canal/foraminal, cavernous, neural/vascular and intracranial interfaces; uncovered or unresolved extent remains unassessed.
steps.look: Review actual apex, optic canal, superior/inferior orbital fissure routes, cavernous region, covered optic pathway/brain/dura and relevant vessels. Contrast, diffusion and vascular acquisitions are separate source evidence; no filling defect, thrombosis, perineural extension or intact interface is assumed from unacquired or inadequate images.
findings: Source apical/canal/foraminal/cavernous and intracranial relation [ ]; obtained extent and uncertainty [ ].
Actual contrast/vascular evidence and differential [ ]; unperformed or unassessed information [ ].
steps.tip: Apparent apical crowding or venous change must be communicated in actual source/clinical context. Unassessed canal, cavernous or intracranial regions cannot become negative extension or vascular-patency statements.

steps.label: Bones and sinuses
steps.detail: Describe each source-supported orbital wall/defect, herniated tissue and adjacent sinus/collection relation; imaging configuration is distinct from clinical entrapment or infection causality.
steps.look: Review actual bony source/reformat planes, every fracture/defect and source herniated fat/muscle/other tissue, adjacent sinuses and collections. Distinguish source morphology from clinical motility/entrapment, globe-pressure state or causal infectious route; prior surgery, artifact and uncovered anatomy remain explicit.
findings: Each source wall/fracture/defect and herniated component [ ]; local measurement and uncertainty [ ].
Clinical entrapment/motility evidence if supplied [ ]; source morphology alone is insufficient [ ].
Actual sinus/collection relationship and supported extension route [ ]; causal/clinical uncertainty [ ].
steps.tip: A muscle near or through a fracture is not proof of clinical entrapment. Sinus opacification does not alone prove the cause of an orbital process; trace actual supported interfaces and limits.

model.reporting_aim: Partial orbital orientation only. This schematic does not supply native globe layers, all muscle/tendon/nerve/sheath/canal/vascular routes, source lesions/trauma/device or intracranial extent, unique histology or visual/motility/pressure function. Actual acquired sources and unassessed anatomy remain explicit.

steps.label: Sinus distribution
steps.detail: Describe each actually covered sinus/compartment and source lesion/secretions/mucosa with extent, modality and uncertainty.
steps.look: Review every covered side/sinus, including actual frontal/maxillary/sphenoid/ethmoid subdivisions and variants. Trace full source lesion/secretions/mucosal boundaries on obtained sequences/windows; record unilateral/bilateral pattern and unassessed extent.
findings: Mucosal thickening of the [maxillary] sinuses bilaterally.
Unilateral complete opacification of the [ ] sinus (consider obstructing lesion or fungal disease).
Air–fluid level in the [ ] sinus.
steps.tip: A low-signal MRI sinus is not automatically aerated; protein-rich/fungal/blood material may simulate air. Hyperdensity or high T2 signal alone does not establish benignity, organism or absence of tumour.

steps.label: Drainage pathways and nasal cavity
steps.detail: Trace source-resolved drainage/nasal routes, obstruction and variants without assuming visible aeration proves functional patency.
steps.look: Inspect actual ostia/recesses/infundibular/nasal/choanal routes, turbinates/septum and relevant variants with the acquired source resolution. Contact/opacification is not a complete 3D tract or measured flow; unacquired CT/endoscopic information remains unavailable.
findings: Obstruction of the [left] ostiomeatal unit.
Nasal polyps filling the nasal cavity.
Periapical lucency of the [ ] molar with maxillary sinusitis (odontogenic source).
steps.tip: MRI anatomy/visible lumen does not alone prove complete drainage patency; low resolution or overlap must remain explicit. Use each actual source and variant, not an inherited generic sinus outline.

steps.label: Operative anatomy and variants
steps.detail: Assess actual operative landmarks/variants with appropriate acquired thin-bone source; do not infer absent dehiscence from unassessed or unresolved MRI.
steps.look: Use actually obtained thin-section bone imaging for relevant skull-base/lateral-lamella/foveal, lamina-papyracea and optic/carotid-canal relationships. Record measured source planes/calibration, asymmetry and uncertainty rather than forcing a normal or operative-risk category.
findings: Asymmetric ethmoid roof, lower on the [ ].
Dehiscent lamina papyracea on the [ ].
Onodi cell with the optic nerve running through it.
Dehiscent carotid canal in the sphenoid sinus.
steps.tip: MRI soft-tissue detail cannot substitute for unacquired/unresolved thin-bone integrity. Partial volume can mimic defects; a missing wall on one image is not confirmed dehiscence or a normal operative variant.

steps.label: Focal tissue and bone
steps.detail: Describe each source tissue/bone component and acquired signal/enhancement/diffusion/CT bone response with technique and differential.
steps.look: Distinguish source signal from true aeration, proteinaceous material, blood/fungal or solid components using actual pre/postcontrast T1/T2/other sequences, CT windows and DWI/ADC if obtained. Separate remodelling/sclerosis/calcification/dehiscence/destruction and marrow replacement.
findings: Enhancing mass with a convoluted cerebriform pattern (inverted papilloma pattern).
Expansile non-enhancing sinus with thinned walls (mucocele).
Destructive enhancing mass with restricted diffusion (malignancy to be excluded).
steps.tip: Enhancement/diffusion/CT morphology can overlap across inflammation, secretions and neoplasia. DWI needs actual ADC/source technique; no unique histology, restricted diffusion or quantitative values are borrowed from unperformed sequences.

steps.label: Extension beyond the sinus
steps.detail: Trace every source-supported extrasinus interface/route and uncertainty, separating visible morphology from histological/perineural/microbial confirmation.
steps.look: Inspect covered orbital walls/compartments/apex, pterygopalatine/infratemporal/masticator routes, foramina/cranial nerves, skull-base marrow, cavernous sinus, dura/brain and adjacent soft tissues. Report every actual source extent/connection and unavailable contrast/diffusion or thin-bone information.
findings: Orbital subperiosteal abscess.
Extension into the pterygopalatine fossa.
Dural enhancement / epidural abscess.
steps.tip: No extrasinus extension is asserted absent from unassessed anatomy. Perineural, orbital/cavernous or intracranial findings require appropriate source extent and clinical correlation; urgency or diagnosis is not inferred solely from the teaching-case label.

model.reporting_aim: Partial sinonasal orientation only. This companion does not supply native patient drainage routes/functional patency, all thin bone/optic/carotid/nerve interfaces, source lesions, perineural or intracranial extent, histology or organism. Actual acquired MRI/CT/clinical sources and unassessed anatomy remain explicit.

steps.label: Oral phase
steps.detail: Assess bolus control, preparation and transfer.
steps.look: Lateral fluoroscopy of the oral cavity with each consistency.
steps.normal: Normal bolus control and transfer; no oral residue.
findings: Premature spillage of liquid into the pharynx before the swallow.
Oral residue after the swallow.

steps.label: Pharyngeal phase
steps.detail: Describe swallow initiation, pharyngeal propulsion and clearance.
steps.look: Lateral and frontal views of the pharynx during the swallow.
steps.normal: Timely swallow initiation with complete pharyngeal clearance.
findings: Delayed swallow initiation with bolus in the pyriform sinuses.
Residue in the valleculae and pyriform sinuses [bilateral / asymmetric].
steps.tip: Asymmetric residue on the frontal view suggests unilateral pharyngeal weakness.

steps.label: Airway protection
steps.detail: Record penetration or aspiration, its timing and the cough response.
steps.look: Lateral view of the larynx during each swallow; note before, during or after the swallow.
findings: Laryngeal penetration to the vocal folds, cleared.
Silent aspiration of thin liquid [during] the swallow (no cough).
Aspiration after the swallow from pyriform sinus residue.
steps.tip: Silent aspiration — without cough — carries the greatest risk; state the cough response.

steps.label: Structural findings
steps.detail: Assess pharyngeal pouches, webs, osteophytes and upper oesophageal sphincter opening.
steps.look: Lateral view of the pharyngo-oesophageal segment.
steps.normal: No diverticulum, web or cricopharyngeal impression.
findings: Zenker diverticulum __ mm above the cricopharyngeus.
Prominent cricopharyngeal bar narrowing the lumen by __%.
Postcricoid web.
Anterior cervical osteophytes indenting the pharynx.

steps.label: Manoeuvres and limitations
steps.detail: Record the response to tested modifications and incomplete coverage.
steps.look: Document each consistency and manoeuvre tested and whether the cervical oesophagus was assessed.
steps.normal: Consistencies tested: [ ]. No manoeuvres required. Cervical oesophagus clear.
findings: Chin-tuck eliminated aspiration of thin liquid.
Thickened liquid swallowed safely.
Examination limited by [patient cooperation / positioning].

steps.label: External and middle ear
steps.detail: Describe each covered canal, membrane, ossicular component/joint, middle-ear compartment and source lesion with actual side, extent and resolution limits.
steps.look: Review actual thin-section CT planes, sampling and artifact. Follow malleus/incus/stapes components and joints, scutum, membrane, Prussak space and other recesses. Do not replace unresolved tiny structures with a generic ossicular model.
findings: Source soft tissue in [recess/compartment] with scutum/ossicular change [ ]; differential and supplied clinical/MRI evidence [ ].
Each source-resolved ossicular component/joint abnormality or uncertainty [ ].
Source canal wall/exostosis or other focal change [ ].
steps.tip: Middle-ear soft tissue and scutum/ossicular change support a differential but do not alone prove cholesteatoma or unique tissue identity. Clinical/otoscopic and acquired MRI evidence remain separate.

steps.label: Mastoid and tegmen
steps.detail: Assess every covered mastoid cell/septum, aditus/antrum, tegmen and cortical interface; separate opacification from source-supported destruction or complication.
steps.look: Review covered mastoid/antral regions, septa, tegmen tympani/mastoideum, inner/outer cortex and adjacent dura/venous interfaces. Distinguish source opacification, prior surgical removal, suspected erosion and acquisition limits.
findings: Mastoid content and each source-supported septal/cortical change [ ]; infection versus postoperative/other differential [ ].
Source tegmen/interface defect or uncertainty [ ]; acquired measurement and adjacent tissue [ ].
Actual postoperative cavity/removal extent and unresolved margins [ ].
steps.tip: Mastoid opacification alone is not proof of coalescent infection. Destruction, extraskeletal extension and adjacent complication need source/clinical support; prior surgery can change expected margins.

steps.label: Inner ear
steps.detail: Trace actual cochlear, vestibular, semicircular, window and aqueduct anatomy with source-resolved bone versus unassessed membranous/neural structures.
steps.look: Use actual canal-aligned and orthogonal CT planes when evaluating suspected dehiscence; record the obtained reformat/measurement basis. Trace each cochlear turn, vestibule, canal/crus/ampulla, window and aqueduct where resolved. MRI fluid/neural detail is a separate acquired source.
findings: Source perifenestral/otic-capsule change [ ]; differential and acquired planes [ ].
Aqueduct morphology [ ]; named source measurement/definition if supported [ ].
Source canal/roof defect or partial-volume uncertainty [ ].
Every actual malformation/variant and obtained extent [ ].
steps.tip: Thin bone and partial volume can mimic canal or roof defects. A canal/aqueduct measurement needs its named site, plane, edge convention and calibration; unassessed membranous or neural anatomy stays unresolved.

steps.label: Facial nerve and vascular channels
steps.detail: Describe each acquired facial/neurovascular canal and adjacent ear interface, variant or defect; a visible bony channel does not establish nerve tissue, vascular flow or integrity.
steps.look: Follow covered labyrinthine/geniculate/tympanic/mastoid facial canal, IAC, carotid/jugular and sigmoid interfaces and actual variants. Describe source bone coverage and uncertainty rather than assuming normal nerve or vessel course/flow.
findings: Each facial canal segment boundary/variant/defect or uncertainty [ ].
Jugular/carotid/sigmoid relation and source-supported variant [ ].
Acquired vascular/neural evidence and missing information [ ].
steps.tip: Suspected exposed/aberrant vascular structures require source-specific characterization and appropriate clinical communication. CT canal shape alone does not establish vessel patency, flow or nerve function.

steps.label: Focal lesion, trauma or device
steps.detail: Map every focal lesion, actual fracture course, postoperative change and device component; report acquired source support, extent, artifact and unresolved relationships.
steps.look: Follow full obtained lesion/fracture/device course and all relevant ear, facial, vascular, skull-base and intracranial interfaces. Record surgical history, device type, source artifact and actually acquired contrast/MRI/DWI/ADC information; do not borrow another case or sequence.
findings: Every obtained fracture course and source ear/neurovascular/intracranial interface [ ].
Every device component/endpoint and source-supported position [ ]; scala/insertion/functional uncertainty [ ].
Each lesion with actually acquired contrast/DWI/anatomical sequences and differential [ ].
steps.tip: CT opacification cannot reliably distinguish all postoperative tissue. Actual non-EPI or suitable multi-shot DWI and anatomical MRI are distinct acquired evidence; small lesions/artifact and mimics limit negative and positive interpretations. Exact electrode scala or insertion extent is not assumed when unresolved.

model.reporting_aim: Partial enlarged temporal-bone orientation only. This schematic does not supply native tiny ossicular/joint/wall geometry, all facial/neurovascular/inner-ear/drainage routes, source lesions, implant scala/endpoints, tissue identity or physiological function. Actual acquired sources and unassessed anatomy remain explicit.

steps.label: Symptom and coverage
steps.detail: Record pulsatile or non-pulsatile tinnitus and side, and whether the protocol covers the right structures.
steps.look: Pulsatile: temporal bone CT and arterial and venous imaging. Non-pulsatile: MRI of the internal auditory canals.
findings: [Right] pulsatile tinnitus: temporal bone CT with CT angiography.
[Left] non-pulsatile tinnitus with hearing loss: MRI of the internal auditory canals.
steps.tip: The work-up depends on whether the tinnitus is pulsatile; say what the protocol can and cannot show.

steps.label: Internal auditory canal and cerebellopontine angle
steps.detail: Inspect the vestibulocochlear nerves and look for a mass.
steps.look: High-resolution T2 and post-contrast T1 of the internal auditory canals.
steps.normal: Internal auditory canals and cerebellopontine angles normal.
findings: Enhancing intracanalicular mass __ × __ × __ mm (vestibular schwannoma pattern).
Vascular loop in the internal auditory canal (common, often incidental).

steps.label: Middle ear and bone
steps.detail: Assess middle ear soft tissue and dehiscence or variants of vascular canals.
steps.look: Temporal bone CT for the jugular bulb, carotid canal and sigmoid plate.
steps.normal: No middle ear mass; normal vascular canals.
findings: Enhancing mass on the cochlear promontory (glomus tympanicum).
Dehiscent sigmoid sinus plate / sigmoid sinus diverticulum.
Dehiscent jugular bulb.

steps.label: Arteries and veins
steps.detail: Review arterial stenosis, dissection, aneurysm and aberrant course, and venous sinus stenosis or diverticulum and signs of shunting.
steps.look: CT or MR angiography and venography; early venous filling as a sign of arteriovenous shunting.
steps.normal: No arterial or venous abnormality; no signs of arteriovenous shunting.
findings: Transverse sinus stenosis (idiopathic intracranial hypertension context).
Carotid dissection / fibromuscular dysplasia.
Early venous filling with enlarged occipital artery branches, suspicious for a dural arteriovenous fistula.
steps.tip: A routine negative MRI does not exclude a dural arteriovenous fistula.

steps.label: Concordance and limits
steps.detail: Match the finding to the side and symptom type and separate a plausible cause from an incidental variant.
steps.look: Side of the finding versus the side of symptoms.
steps.normal: No cause for the tinnitus identified on this protocol.
findings: Ipsilateral [finding] is a plausible cause.
Findings are contralateral / incidental.
Catheter angiography would be needed to exclude a fistula.

steps.label: Thyroid background
steps.detail: Measure both lobes and the isthmus and describe parenchymal echotexture and vascularity.
steps.look: Inspect actual lobe/isthmus planes and encountered variant/ectopic/treated tissue, gland boundaries and source parenchyma. Record actual Doppler acquisition and sampling/coverage limits.
findings: Actual acquired thyroid background findings [ ]; source/identity/extent [ ]; uncertainty and unavailable evidence [ ].
steps.tip: Do not preset a normal-sized homogeneous gland or normal flow without actual adequate acquisition.

steps.label: Nodule location and size
steps.detail: Number each clinically relevant nodule, record side and pole and measure three dimensions.
steps.look: Identify every actual relevant nodule and each internal component; source transverse and longitudinal planes, axes/edge convention, measurement calibration and same-case comparison.
findings: Actual acquired nodule location and size findings [ ]; source/identity/extent [ ]; uncertainty and unavailable evidence [ ].
steps.tip: Stable identifiers and comparable calibrated source planes are required; a selected index image does not inventory every nodule.

steps.label: TI-RADS features and points
steps.detail: Score composition, echogenicity, shape, margin and echogenic foci and add the points.
steps.look: Assess each source-resolved solid/fluid/spongiform component, reference gland/muscle echogenicity, transverse shape, margin and each foci type. Record shadowing and unavailable tissue/feature information.
